precepts.text: The same command word for word: pure oil olive beaten for the light, the lamps ordered from evening unto morning before the Lord continually, a statute for ever.
precepts.point: Though Israel is in captivity now without a temple, without lamps to bring oil for, and no longer under the Levitical priesthood, think about it spiritually: you have to keep your lamp lit and keep the oil in your life. Brotherhood and unity, and correction, which is an excellent oil that shall not break the head, are that oil; if you are not around a body being built up and corrected by teachers and peers, that is how people run out of oil, their lamp goes out, and they fall out of this truth and do not endure to the end. The ten virgins with their lamps and oil come to mind here, offered as a meditation.

note.label: Exodus 27: The Altar, the Court, and the Oil for the Lamp

precepts.why:
Leviticus gives the same command word for word: “Command the children of Israel, that they bring unto thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamps to burn continually. Without the vail of the testimony, in the tabernacle of the congregation, shall Aaron order it from the evening unto the morning before the Lord continually: it shall be a statute for ever in your generations. He shall order the lamps upon the pure candlestick before the Lord continually.”

The children of Israel bring the oil; Aaron and his sons order the lamps from evening to morning before the Lord; and the lamp burns always, a statute for ever unto their generations.

Israel is in captivity now without a temple, without lamps to bring oil for, and no longer under the Levitical priesthood. So think about it spiritually: you have to keep your lamp lit and keep the oil in your life.

precepts.why:
“Let the righteous smite me; it shall be a kindness: and let him reprove me; it shall be an excellent oil, which shall not break my head: for yet my prayer also shall be in their calamities.”

Correction is oil for the lamp, an excellent oil that shall not break the head. Being corrected by teachers and peers in a body that is being built up is what keeps the oil in your life. Without it the lamp goes out, and people fall out of this truth and do not endure to the end.

precepts.text: The children of Israel brought pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always; Aaron and his sons ordered it from evening to morning before the Lord, a statute for ever.
precepts.point: Eli was laid down in his place, his eyes beginning to wax dim, and ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, Samuel was laid down to sleep. Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out. That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out, though at a point in time it did go out.

note.label: 1 Samuel 3: The Lord Reveals Himself to Samuel

precepts.why:
Samuel lay down “ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep.” Ere means before: before the lamp of God went out.

That light in the temple by the ark was never to go out. The children of Israel were to “bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always.” “Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the Lord: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.” Yet at a point in time it did go out.

points: The court of the tabernacle: hangings of fine twined linen an hundred cubits on the south and north sides, fifty on the west and east, with pillars filleted with silver in sockets of brass, and the gate of the court a hanging of blue, purple, and scarlet wrought with needlework. The length of the court a hundred cubits, the breadth fifty every where, the height five cubits, and all the pins of brass.
